rationale: B has a real logic bug. For any straight it sets high = 5 if ranks[0] == 14, so the ace-high straight 10-J-Q-K-A is scored as a five-high straight and would lose to every other straight. A handles the ace-low wheel explicitly, only when ranks == [14, 5, 4, 3, 2]. B also packs its category selection into a six-level chained conditional expression that is hard to read, and uses (rank, count) tuples as tiebreakers, which works but is less clear. A has docstrings, a plain if/elif category selection with comments naming each hand, and clean rank-only tiebreak lists. A builds its counts by hand where collections.Counter would be more idiomatic, but it is correct and clearer.
